strongest_objection: A 3-6 person core cannot run a regulated money operation through December, audits, incidents and absence at the same time. The org chart will be rebuilt after the first bad quarter. The model buys December at +50% premium hours with no capacity limit, and F3 suspends release when one person is absent.
evidence_that_would_answer: A full operating year at a design partner covering December and at least one absence; a roster double-absence test (CNV-GOV-004); December interval arrival data.
answered_by_current_research: Partly. The OPS December model and ADV2 E04 quantify the risk (+$0.2-1.0M/yr; break-even +$0.16-0.36B). Nothing has been observed.

strongest_objection: The research is too pessimistic. It holds 30% incompressible effort, 1,520 productive hours, 7.5% contingency, 10% financing on capital, coordination counted twice, and human controls that a deterministic gate could replace. The build could be under $1M and operations under 30 minutes per account.
evidence_that_would_answer: Measured accepted-capability rates under the DEV protocol; an accepted Rehearsal-type run; an auditor's acceptance of the deterministic gate (CNV-GOV-003) and of generated evidence (CNV-GOV-001).
answered_by_current_research: Partly. Pessimistic biases are real but small: coordination -$0.00-0.04B of break-even (ADV2-013); financing overstates equity need by 16-24% (ADV2-009); the +3% productivity bug (ADV2-014). The only end-to-end trial failed (1/108), so the optimistic case is contradicted, not just unproven.

strongest_objection: Year-5 profit of $0.8-1.1M on $4.3-7.4M of capital, profitable only after 18-42 months, rests on 2-3 sponsors. Incumbents can copy most levers in 6-36 months (COM replication). There is no terminal value, exit evidence or comparable. ROIC is a one-year snapshot of a still-ramping company, and the key-person risk is the founder.
evidence_that_would_answer: Signed LOIs with minimum fees; NPV/IRR with an explicit terminal value; comparable transactions; customer concentration limits.
answered_by_current_research: No. The research reports ROIC on one year (ADV2-009) and does not value the company.

strongest_objection: At $1M+ balances 20 bps costs more than my equivalent-scope in-house cost (COM: 5-10 bps). I still pay oversight ($60k + $7.5/acct), appointees, migration ($150k+), payment rails and the startup's risk. Why switch to an entrant with no SOC history?
evidence_that_would_answer: My own activity costing; a value-share pilot with a measured baseline; the entrant's SOC 1 Type 2 report.
answered_by_current_research: Partly. The COM sponsor-value model is modelled, not observed. Sponsor-side costs are excluded from the model (hidden-cost ledger HC-01/02/06).

strongest_objection: In F3/F5 the controller both releases and reconciles, but CNV-GOV-003 puts reconciliation outside the payment chain. A 200-hour fractional reviewer is thin independence for five sponsor books, and a month-end close across five books with three people has no slack.
evidence_that_would_answer: A control matrix walkthrough by an audit firm; an ITGC design; a timed mock close across multiple books.
answered_by_current_research: No. The model's control check is a head count (ADV2-004).

strongest_objection: OFAC dispositions are never auto-closed. Sanctions recall in the public replay is 88/100. The compliance owner is a 0.25 FTE contractor, and the narrow service sells screening while dropping the compliance consultant. Who clears flags in peak December?
evidence_that_would_answer: Replay recall >= 99% with documented false-negative handling; a named compliance officer; a counsel opinion on money transmission (CNV-LEG-002).
answered_by_current_research: Partly. OPS states the human floors; recall and the opinion are open (ADV2-017).

strongest_objection: We can re-tier selectively at renewal in 0-6 months, add AI triage to our operations, and we already have SOC history and integrations. You are selling to the same 2-5 decision units we serve, and switching is rare (COM: 8 migrations, 6 to Foundant).
evidence_that_would_answer: Win/loss in competitive processes; renewal price moves by incumbents; switching rate history.
answered_by_current_research: Partly. COM replication.csv gives judgement scores; there is no market test.

strongest_objection: Will my December grants clear on time if release stops when someone is absent, or if AI is down? Who do I talk to? Can I take my data with me?
evidence_that_would_answer: A December SLA under an absence + AI outage stress (OPS scenario); service history at a design partner; an export test.
answered_by_current_research: No. OPS models a backlog of 51,000 minutes at 31 December under annual sizing, and no SLA is evidenced.

strongest_objection: I cannot rely on an AI-authored codebase with one human maintainer and no SAST or dependency scanning in any Echelon repo. A deterministic gate counts as releaser only with ITGCs effective over a period. Generated evidence needs IPE support. Type 2 needs 6-12 months of operation.
evidence_that_would_answer: The auditor's planned-approach letter; an ITGC design walkthrough; a SOC readiness assessment focused on agent-made changes.
answered_by_current_research: No. DEV and LYR list it as an evidence gap.
